rules.statement: The frontmatter description names when to use the skill and what it does, under 1024 characters; 'when to use' signals belong in the description, not only the body.
rules.reason: The description is the primary triggering mechanism; clarity there is worth more than body prose.
rules.proof: Every description contains a trigger phrase and stays under 1024 characters.

rules.statement: Skills contain no project law, product names, private tooling, or broken relative links; sibling skills are referenced by name.
rules.reason: Portability is this repo's public contract.
rules.proof: A token sweep for internal names returns only intentional examples; repo-internal links resolve.

rules.statement: Keep SKILL.md focused on the procedure (under roughly 500 lines); move reference material to references/ or examples/ one hop away.
rules.reason: Agents load the body on trigger; large artifacts belong one hop away.
rules.proof: No SKILL.md exceeds 500 lines; large artifacts live in subdirectories.

rules.statement: When two skills overlap or pair, each 'when NOT to use' section names the sibling and the boundary once, instead of duplicating procedure.
rules.reason: Clear boundaries keep the set composable without repeated instruction.
rules.proof: Each overlapping pair names the other by name in a when-not line.

documentation.label: One owner, one fact, clear job

rules.statement: Put each durable fact in one owner; other documents state only their local consequence and link to that owner.
rules.reason: One authority is easier to retrieve, update, and verify than copied guidance.
rules.proof: Every changed claim has one owner and an exact link.

rules.statement: Keep an example only when it encodes a requirement or repairs a measured failure.
rules.reason: Canonical examples teach behavior without turning prose into an edge-case list.
rules.proof: Each retained example names the behavior it protects.

responses.label: Answer, evidence, and one next move
responses.scope: agent and human handoffs from this repository

rules.statement: Lead with the answer or decision before the process narrative.
rules.reason: The reader should know what changed without excavating the work log.
rules.proof: The first sentence answers the user's question or names the current state.

rules.statement: Use the compact shape: answer, up to three proved results, one next action, and one bounded request only when blocked.
rules.reason: A stable response shape reduces coordination cost without hiding proof.
rules.proof: Routine updates fit on one screen and expose the next edge.
